subject: Strategies for variation in seasonal abundance

messages.author: 985e455b8390aae3
messages.subject: Strategies for variation in seasonal abundance
parts:
I'm interested in assessing seasonal variation in abundance of snakes at 18 sites.  I've got pcount running swimmingly (aside from no SE predictions for the ZIP mixture), but with no effect of season (wet/dry) included anywhere.

My data were collected in a seasonally-balanced fashion (half of sampling in each season) but not at all sites during the same seasons (spread across ~30 months).

Does anyone care to comment on the following strategy options, or offer something I haven't thought of?:

1.  pcountOpen, on first blush, seems to be the appropriate method, but I'm unclear as to how to format the data.  Would my primary periods be DRY1, WET1, DRY2, WET2, DRY3, WET3, with very uneven sampling during secondary periods (lots of NAs) for sites that were not sampled during some of these periods? Would the model still be valid without sampling all sites in all seasons?  If so, would a catvar "season," then, be my gammaformula and omegaformula? 

2.  It seems like crass pseudo-replication, but should I estimate abundance for each site/season pairing independently, i.e., turn my 18 sites into SITE1WET, SITE1DRY, SITE2WET...for 36 separate "site" estimates?  Might I then consider "season" as a site covariate?  Ugh, it pains me to even suggest it.

3.  Maybe even worse, should I just consider season as an observation covariate?  This conditions on the same N for each site regardless of season, and if snakes are actually emigrating seasonally then the observation model is being informed by two different realizations of the Poisson.  Then again, maybe snakes aren't moving in or out but are just more or less active, in which case a seasonal effect on p would be appropriate. 

Please don't hesitate to be honest about my naivete on the issues.

Shane
